heroLead: Montezuma Creek sits within the Aneth Field's productive footprint, directly on the Navajo Nation, where the Ute Mountain Ute and Navajo Nation boundaries both come into play.
intro: Montezuma Creek is a small community in far southeastern San Juan County, close to both the Aneth Field's core production and the point where the Navajo Nation and Ute Mountain Ute reservation boundaries meet. Mineral ownership in this specific pocket of the state is layered in a way that requires careful confirmation — tribal trust land from two different tribal jurisdictions can sit near privately held fee minerals within a short distance.

We buy privately held fee mineral and royalty interests near Montezuma Creek. Given the complexity of ownership in this area, we confirm status thoroughly before making any offer, and we will tell you directly if your interest falls outside what we can purchase.

sections.heading: Where two reservation boundaries meet
paragraphs: This corner of San Juan County sits close to both Navajo Nation and Ute Mountain Ute trust land, in addition to privately held minerals, which makes careful title and status confirmation especially important here. We do not guess based on general area reputation — we check the specific record tied to your legal description before discussing anything.

sections.heading: Direct exposure to Aneth Field production
paragraphs: For privately held interests confirmed to be in fee status, proximity to the Aneth Field's long-producing carbonate reservoir generally means there is a substantial production history to draw on. We pull that history directly from Utah Division of Oil, Gas and Mining records tied to your specific well or unit before building an offer.

sections.heading: What to send us first
paragraphs: If you believe your family holds a privately owned interest near Montezuma Creek, the most useful starting point is any deed, patent, or division order you have, along with whatever family history you know about how the land was acquired. That background helps us determine status accurately and move efficiently once ownership is confirmed.

faqs.question: How complicated is confirming ownership status near Montezuma Creek?
faqs.answer: More involved than most areas, since both Navajo Nation and Ute Mountain Ute trust land are nearby. We do this confirmation work as a first step before any offer.

faqs.answer: We will tell you directly and point you to the Bureau of Indian Affairs process, since we only purchase privately held fee interests.

faqs.question: Is there strong production history for confirmed fee interests here?
faqs.answer: Often yes, given the proximity to the long-producing Aneth Field, and we use that history directly when building an offer.
